contests.title: QUESTION #1: Increasing the Timeframe for the Hawaii Senate to Consider and Act on Judicial Appointments.

provenance.quote:
QUESTION #1: Increasing the Timeframe for the Hawaii Senate to Consider and Act on Judicial Appointments.
Shall the Constitution of the State of Hawaii be amended to allow the Senate more time to consider and act on the appointments of justices and judges, by increasing the timeframe from thirty days to sixty days for appointments made between April 1 and December 31 when the senate is not in regular session or is about to adjourn the regular session?

contests.title: QUESTION #2: Directing the Hawaii State Legislature to Establish Procedures for Counties to Issue RISE Bonds, Exempt from County Debt Limits.

provenance.quote:
QUESTION #2: Directing the Hawaii State Legislature to Establish Procedures for Counties to Issue RISE Bonds, Exempt from County Debt Limits.
Shall the Hawaii State Constitution be amended to direct the legislature to authorize the counties to issue resilient infrastructure for shelter and equity bonds to fund public improvements in designated districts, repaid solely by future growth in property tax revenues within those districts, not by increasing real property tax rates, where such bonds are excluded from the counties’ debt limit and are subject to accountability and oversight requirements as may be provided by law?

Charter Question #1
Should the Charter require annual funding for a Food Security Fund, without having to simultaneously increase real property tax rates to fund the appropriation, to support programs and grants that provide locally grown or produced food to Oahu residents, as well as non-local food only in an emergency?

Charter Question #2
Should the Charter be amended to replace its preamble with language recognizing the relationship between the people of the City and County of Honolulu and the 'aina, honoring the wisdom of kupuna and the legacy of Prince Jonah Kuhio Kalaniana'ole, and affirming commitments to transparent, accountable government and stewardship of natural, civic, and cultural resources?

Charter Question #3
Should an Office of 'Oiwi Resources and Cultural Stewardship be established within the Office of the Mayor to oversee the management of 'Oiwi resources within the City, develop related programs, and create a Cultural Advisory Council of kupuna, cultural practitioners, and community representatives?

Charter Question #4
Should a nine-member LGBTQIA+ Commission be established to advise the Mayor, City Council, and City agencies on matters affecting the LGBTQIA+ community and recommend policies, programs, and legislation promoting social, economic, and political equality?

Charter Question #5
Beginning in 2032, should the City use ranked-choice voting to elect the Mayor, City Council, and Prosecuting Attorney, allowing voters to rank candidates in the order they prefer (1st, 2nd, 3rd, etc.) in a single November election?

Charter Question #6
Should the Charter be amended to require the Honolulu Police Department to 1) adopt policies to ensure the constitutional rights of all persons regardless of immigration or citizenship status are protected, and 2) assist federal immigration enforcement activities only when required by statute or court order, and after the requesting agency's identity and authority have been confirmed?

Charter Question #7
Shall the Revised Charter of the City and County of Honolulu be amended to encourage increasing housing availability and preserving available housing as policies for the City and County of Honolulu?

Charter Question #8
Should the Charter be amended to clarify that the Affordable Housing Fund is a revolving fund, with repayments, interest, earnings, proceeds, and other receipts derived from the Fund to be redeposited into the Fund?

Charter Question #9
Should the Charter be amended to no longer require a second public hearing for any transaction related to City real property interests?

Charter Question #10
Should the City be required to prepare and carry out a functional plan for the development of affordable housing?

Charter Question #11
Should the Charter be amended to allow the Clean Water and Natural Lands Fund and the Climate Resiliency Fund to award grants to federal income tax-exempt nonprofit organizations that provide services that are consistent with each Fund's purpose?

Charter Question #12
Should the Revised City Charter be amended to allow the Clean Water and Natural Lands Fund, Affordable Housing Fund, Climate Resiliency Fund, and other funds established under Section 9-204 to receive funding from federal, state, philanthropic, and other sources?

Charter Question #13
Should the Charter be amended to allow the Clean Water and Natural Lands Fund to be used for historic preservation, and to preserve and protect buildings, sites, structures, and objects that have been acquired by the fund; to rename the Fund the Land, Natural Resources, and Historic Preservation Fund, and the advisory commission for the Fund the Land, Natural Resources, and Historic Preservation advisory commission; and to allocate proposal review for Fund use between the advisory commission and the O'ahu Historic Preservation Commission?

Charter Question #14
Should the Charter be amended to increase the annual appropriation for costs related to operation, maintenance, and management of lands that were acquired using the Clean Water and Natural Lands Fund, from 5% of the moneys that were deposited into the Fund in the previous year, to 10%?

Charter Question #15
Should an Office of Data and Innovation be established to use data to improve city services, promote government transparency and civic engagement, ensure that the city uses artificial intelligence responsibly, and protect residents' digital privacy?

Charter Question #16
Should permanent resident aliens who are residents of the City and County of Honolulu be permitted to serve on City boards and commissions?

Charter Question #17
Should quorum and board action be based on the majority of members eligible to vote, excluding vacancies and non-voting members?

Charter Question #18
Should the First Deputy of the Department of Human Resources be exempt from civil service provisions, like similar roles in other City departments?

Charter Question #19
Should the City Clerk be required to provide technical and secretarial services to the Charter Commission?

Charter Question #20
Should the Charter make a Councilmember, the Mayor, or the Prosecuting Attorney ineligible for election to any City office for two years if impeached, or if the official resigns after an impeachment petition has been filed, consistent with the provision for being recalled from office?

contests.title: 1. Hawai‘i: County Auditor's Power to Employ

provenance.quote:
1. Hawai‘i: County Auditor's Power to Employ
Shall the Hawai'i County Charter be amended to allow the County Auditor to hire a deputy and exercise the same power, with respect to the employees within the Auditor's office, as the department heads in the executive branch?

contests.title: Maui: Planning Commission Review of General Plan and Land Use Ordinances

provenance.quote:
Maui: Planning Commission Review of General Plan and Land Use Ordinances
Shall the Charter be amended, effective January 2, 2027, to provide clarity and consistency in deadlines for planning commission review of revisions to the general plan, zoning ordinances, and other land use ordinances proposed by the council, and transmittal of related findings and recommendations to the council?

contests.title: Maui: Standardizing Deadlines for Voter Initiative, Recall, and Charter Amendment

provenance.quote:
Maui: Standardizing Deadlines for Voter Initiative, Recall, and Charter Amendment
Shall the Charter be amended, effective January 1, 2027, to standardize the deadlines related to the clerk's processing of petitions related to voter initiative, recall of elected officers or board or commission members, and charter amendments?

Maui: Computation of Time
Shall the Charter be amended, effective January 1, 2027, to establish a formula for computing Charter deadlines that excludes weekends and holidays?

Maui: Processing of Claims
Shall the Charter be amended, effective January 1, 2028 to streamline the process for filing claims for personal injury or property damage by requiring that claims are filed directly with the Director of Finance or as provided by ordinance?

contests.title: Maui: Removing the English Translation of the Hawai‘i State Motto

provenance.quote:
Maui: Removing the English Translation of the Hawai‘i State Motto
Shall the Charter be amended, effective upon passage, by removing the English translation of the Hawai'i State motto in the Maui County Charter Preamble, allowing the original phrase, “Ua mau ke ea o ka ‘aina i ka pono,” to stand on its own?

Maui: Emergency Appropriations
Shall the Charter be amended, effective January 2, 2027, to allow the Mayor, with approval from the Council, to pass an emergency appropriation for an application for a line of credit and clarify that the one percent limitation for emergency appropriations does not apply to funds that have already been allocated to an emergency fund?

Maui: Independent Nomination Board
Shall the Charter be amended, effective immediately, to repeal the parts of the 2022 Charter amendment that created the Independent Nomination Board and related procedures for nominations for various County officers?

contests.title: Maui: Reappointment of Members of the Board of Ethics

provenance.quote:
Maui: Reappointment of Members of the Board of Ethics
Shall the Charter be amended, effective upon approval, to authorize the Mayor to reappoint members of the Board of Ethics of the County of Maui, with the approval of the Council, for one successive term without an intervening waiting period?

contests.title: Relating to the Planning Commission’s Appeals Process

provenance.quote:
Relating to the Planning Commission’s Appeals Process
Shall the Kaua’i County Charter be amended to expedite and clarify the Planning Commission's appeals process by removing all references to a Zoning Board of Appeals?

coverageNotes: The complete official Candidate Report CSV contains 415 filing records. Only candidates with status In General are included. 29 state legislative contests were decided at the primary and are recorded as absences.

The two statewide constitutional questions are taken verbatim from the Office of Elections. Both official full texts were acquired from the Legislature. Its reports link the enrolled bill PDFs and match the bill identifiers and original links on the election-office question page; each printed PDF question matches the held question after typography and whitespace normalization.

The Governor and Lieutenant Governor form two joint ticket choices. All 140 people listed In General in the complete official Candidate Report are represented, including the 44 local candidates. Official sample ballots supply 20 Honolulu, eight Maui, one Hawaii and one Kauai county charter questions.

sources.reviewedEvidence: Native official CSV export; all filing records acquired, November candidacies filtered by In General status; printed ballot names, parties and websites preserved; mailing addresses excluded.
Official public Candidate Report grid supplies the total filing count used to verify the full CSV export.
Official 2026 contest schedule validates all legislative districts and term lengths, identifies three at-large OHA seats and places U.S. Senate in 2028.
Official statewide constitutional-amendment page supplies both question titles, verbatim ballot questions, and linked full-text measures.

Official November 3, 2026 precinct 01-01 general-election ballot prints one Governor and Lieutenant Governor contest with two joint choices; OCR verifies every pairing against the complete official CSV.

Official 2026 Candidate’s Manual, printed page 24: In the Primary Election, Governor and Lieutenant Governor are each a separate contest. However, in the General Election, Governor and Lieutenant Governor are voted for as a team by political party or as a team by nonpartisan.

Official 2026 news release identifies the Candidate Report as the official candidate list: Following the candidate filing deadline, election officials will then finalize the list of candidates for the 2026 Elections and begin preparing ballots based on each voter’s district.
Official Candidate Reports page states filing is closed and links the public candidate report, last updated September 4, 2026.

Official full text of SB121, linked from the Legislature report whose measure status link exactly matches the election-office full-text link. The printed ballot question matches the election-office question after whitespace and typographic quote normalization.

Official Legislature report identifies the final measure label, links its full-text PDF, and records Enrolled to Governor: SB121 Justices and Judges; Appointment; Confirmation; Constitutional Amendment (ConAm) PROPOSING AN AMENDMENT TO ARTICLE VI, SECTION 3, OF THE HAWAII STATE CONSTITUTION TO ALLOW THE SENATE MORE TIME TO CONFIRM JUDICIAL APPOINTMENTS. Proposes an amendment to the Hawaii State Constitution to extend the amount of time allowed the Senate to consider and act on the appointments of justices and judges from thirty to sixty days for appointments made between April 1 and December 31 when the Senate is not in Regular Session or is about to adjourn the Regular Session. (S) 4/4/2025- Enrolled to Governor. RHOADS, KANUHA, KIDANI JHA, FIN
